translations.answer: In the symmetric sagittal plane setup of Sigmaban, the FRASA uses a five-degree-of-freedom CrossQ/SAC strategy to unify prone/supine stand-up and sagittal pendulum disturbance recovery, and it is faster than KFB in repeated real-robot trials; this conclusion does not cover side, asymmetric, large robots, or long-term mechanical fatigue, and manual screening of high-stress strategies is still required before deployment.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The target robot has validated left-right symmetry for the controlled joints.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Actuator delays, gains, force bounds, friction and thermal behavior are re-identified for the deployment robot.
translations.confidence_rationale: Repeated real-robot stand-up and pendulum comparisons plus public environment code support the narrow result. Confidence is capped by one small robot, sagittal symmetry, manual candidate selection and unreported long-term mechanical loads.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines the symmetric end-to-end policy and reports repeated real stand-up and pendulum recovery comparisons.
translations.evidence.0.title: FRASA: An End-to-End Reinforcement Learning Agent for Fall Recovery and Stand Up of Humanoid Robots
translations.evidence.1.locator: StandupEnv.apply_control, get_observation, step, apply_randomization and randomize_fall at 78457df
translations.evidence.1.note: Maps the five-DoF interface, incremental control, termination, dynamics randomization and fallen-state initialization to official code.
translations.evidence.1.title: Rhoban/frasa official implementation
translations.safety.command_limits: Identify robot-specific joint position/speed, actuator torque/current/temperature, impact and control-rate envelopes; the paper's 4-7.3 J impacts are test conditions, not ratings.
translations.safety.emergency_stop: Verify an independent emergency stop and safe torque-off response before supported or disturbance testing.
translations.safety.protective_controls: Use a tether or padded capture where compatible, an exclusion zone, a repeatable low-energy disturbance rig, thermal/current monitoring and post-trial mechanical inspection.
translations.safety.robot_specific_warning: Evidence is specific to the 70 cm, 7.5 kg Sigmaban and symmetric sagittal control; larger robots, lateral falls and asymmetrical contacts require a new design review.
translations.safety.staged_deployment: Validate terminations and self-collision in simulation, then supported low-speed prone/supine motions, low-energy disturbances, and only then bounded unsupported trials; do not perform online exploration on unprotected hardware.
translations.title: Can a lightweight strategy unify fall recovery and stand-up in humanoid robots?
